newsitem.title: USA: CIA official charged with spying for Russia.
newsitem.headline: CIA official charged with spying for Russia.

text.p: CIA employee Harold Nicholson was formally charged on Monday with conspiring to spy for Russia since June 1994 in exchange for more than $100,000.

A criminal complaint, filed in federal court in Virginia three days ago and made public Monday, alleged that Nicholson -- a CIA employee since 1982 -- conspired to violate the espionage laws by passing classified information to Russian agents.
According to the charges, Nicholson just six days ago photographed secret and top-secret CIA documents about Russia with the intention of delivering them to a Russian intelligence officer.
FBI agent Michael Lonergan charged in an affidavit that Nicholson "has been acting clandestinely, corruptly and illegally as an agent of the Russian Federation foreign intelligence service."

Nicholson was taken into custody on Saturday at Washington's Dulles Airport. The affidavit was filed to support the arrest warrant and searches of his residence, his workspace at the CIA, his car, his bank safe deposit box and his luggage.

Nicholson, who turned 46 on Sunday, had access to some of the nation's most sensitive intelligence secrets. He had been an operations officer in various posts around the world, and worked as an instructor at a classified CIA special training center between 1994 and 1996.
